newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai copper futures end down in slow trade.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai copper futures end down in slow trade.

text.p: Shanghai copper futures ended down in slow trade on Thursday with investors shortage of any reason to buy given poor fundamentals, traders said.

The most actively traded September 1997 contract ended at 23,370 ($2,818) yuan per tonne, down 90 yuan from Wednesday's close. It opened at an intraday high of 23,400 yuan and hit a low of 23,300 yuan per tonne.
June fell 50 to 22,700 yuan per tonne, July 110 to 22,890, August 100 to 23,130, October 70 to 23,430 and November 110 to 23,410 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume rose slightly to 35,390 tonnes from 34,980.

Speculative buying was not active though some short-covering emerged at the 23,300 yuan level as big domestic copper producers were seen selling heavily due to unfavourable fundamentals, traders said.
Flat domestic demand was compounded by falls in exports of copper and copper products, and this had led to oversupply on the local market, they said.
April exports of uncast copper and copper products were 13,494 tonnes, down 17.35 percent from March, the China Securities newspaper said early this week.
Domestic copper consumers are generally short of cash and so are having to curtail their copper purchases, traders said.
"Those big shorts continued selling and most of them are major copper producers, so that has led to some heavy selling pressure at high levels," one trader said.
The price of physical copper is around 22,900 yuan per tonne in the Shanghai area, down from 23,100 yuan early this week, traders said.
Aluminium ended mostly up. June rose 30 to 14,950 yuan per tonne, July fell 20 to 15,000, August did not trade, September rose 150 to 15,350 and October 100 to 15,300 yuan per tonne.
Combined volume fell to 1,340 tonnes from 1,530 tonnes on Wednesday.
